subject: Recap + next steps: token bands, budget range & feature payback (CareWell)
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elaine Kim <elaine.kim@carewell.ai>, Sam Torres <sam.torres@carewell.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Oct 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + next steps: token bands, budget range & feature payback (CareWell)

Hi Elaine / Sam —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap while it’s fresh and a proposed set of next steps so we can get you a concrete pilot proposal.

Call highlights
- Primary use case: in-product conversational assistant + short summarization for provider notes.
- Expected volume (initial cohort): 3–5M tokens/month across 150 active users; scale to ~12–18M tokens/month in 9–12 months.
- Timing: pilot in November, production beta Jan–Feb.

Preliminary commercial constraints you shared
- Target paid price range (ballpark): $200–$350 per 1M tokens (customer-side budget).
- Payback: team wants feature-level CAC payback inside 9 months, ideal closer to 6.
- Margin targets: product owners want >=30% gross margin after inference cost across paid tier.
- Security: PII redaction and audit logs mandatory for pilot.

What we propose next (short list)
1) Fill and return the attached unit_econ_template.xlsx with per-feature monthly token estimates (I pre-filled the assistant + summary rows).
2) We’ll run an internal unit-econ deep-dive and return a recommended pricing band that meets your margin and payback targets (within 3 business days of receiving the sheet).
3) Technical pilot: 1M token smoke test (hosted) to validate latency/quality and infer costs — we’ll provide a scoped SOW and SLA addendum.
4) Security checklist: please send over the internal security contact; we’ll attach SOC2 evidence and our privacy spec.

Questions for you (please confirm)
- Is the 3–5M/month initial band representative of the first 3 months or steady-state?
- For CAC calculations: what is your expected ARPU or incremental revenue per user from the assistant feature? A rough number is fine.

I attached the unit_econ_template.xlsx and a short one-pager of the commercial cadence we typically run. Ben / Marissa — flagged for pricing alignment and to schedule a technical deep-dive next week.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for a 30-min pricing alignment meeting.

Best,
Ava Chen

Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: token bands, budget range & feature payback (CareWell)

Thanks Ava — good recap. A couple quick clarifications:

- The 3–5M/month estimate is for the first 60 days of pilot (we expect active users and tokens to ramp). Steady-state for the initial rollout is probably closer to the 8–10M/month range you mentioned for month 3.
- On the price band: our procurement team gave a target of $200–$350 per 1M tokens, but that’s fluid — lower price if you can guarantee caching/prefix reuse and bounded latency.
- Security: I’m attaching our Security_QA_CareWell.pdf with the questions we’ll want answered before pilot sign-off (PII handling, logging, KMS). Our InfoSec lead is Sam (cc’d).

Regarding CAC payback: we don’t have a hard ARPU yet. For scoping the payback math I can share conversion assumptions after I sync with RevOps — aim is <9 months, ideally 6 for a fast-moving pilot.

I’ll try to get the unit econ sheet back by Thursday EOD.

Best,
Elaine
Director of Product, CareWell
elaine.kim@carewell.ai

Elaine — appreciate the quick turnaround and the security doc. A few notes from commercial: 

- We can price both Hosted and Dedicated variants. For initial pilot we usually propose Hosted with a pilot discount; for steady-state we provide a graduated band that drops as you hit higher bands (8–12M and 12M+).
- To meet a $200–$350 target while protecting margin, we’d recommend:
  • aggressive prefix/KV cache configuration for the assistant to reduce tokens billed,
  • a quantization-aware model variant for batch inference on long-running summarization jobs,
  • and optionally a reserved-capacity commit if you expect to move to steady-state in Q1.

Action items I’ll own:
- Draft a proposed_pricing_matrix.pdf that maps token bands to list/discounted pricing and shows modeled margin and CAC payback for three sample ARPU scenarios (I’ll attach).
- Book a technical deep-dive with infra/PM (Marissa) to validate latency and caching opportunities — suggested times sent via calendar.

Elaine — if you can share even a rough ARPU assumption, I’ll include the CAC payback math in the matrix.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

Thanks all — next steps confirmed below and a quick unit-econ sketch so you can see the shape of the recommendation we’ll return once we get your filled template.

Confirmed next steps
- Elaine -> return unit_econ_template.xlsx (ETA: Thu EOD) and share any ARPU guidance.
- Ben -> deliver proposed_pricing_matrix.pdf with modeled margins & CAC payback (ETA: Mon Oct 9).
- Marissa -> technical deep-dive to scope caching and latency tradeoffs (calendar invite sent).
- InfoSec -> Redwood will provide SOC2 artifact and KMS integration notes (we will upload to the Drive link below).

Mini unit-econ sketch (illustrative only)
- Feature: Conversational assistant (per active user)
  • Assumptions: avg tokens/user/month = 900k tokens (active users = 150) -> 135M tokens/month at scale (this is a long-term projection).
  • Inference cost (our internal infra estimate for the recommended model/config): ~$0.85 per 1M tokens.
  • List price target (example): $250 per 1M tokens -> gross margin on inference line = 250 - 0.85 ≈ $249.15 per 1M tokens (~>99% gross margin vs raw token compute), but note this oversimplifies — we model caching/reuse, sequence-length distribution, and ops costs which drive effective per-customer margin down to target ~30% after total cost backs.
  • CAC payback example: if incremental ARPU per user/month = $40, then payback at 900k tokens/user/month (with pricing above) is approximately 7–8 months (model will be included in Ben’s matrix).

Notes on the cost line above: the $0.85 figure is a conservative internal estimator for amortized GPU cost + runtime overhead for the specific model we discussed. The unit_econ_template will let us do per-feature and per-customer cohort math to produce a concrete $/feature and payback timeline that maps to your ARPU assumptions.

Drive + records
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cExampleLink (I’ll upload SOC2, KMS notes, and the filled econ worksheet).
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/479201/CW-2028-042

If that looks good I’ll start the pilot SOW draft after we get the filled sheet.

Thanks — Ava
